ask.ifNot: 30 is close, but 4 does not go into 30. 60 works for all four: 2, 4, 5 and 6.

beats.say: In sixtieths: one half is 30 over 60, one quarter is 15 over 60, 1 over 5 is 12 over 60, and 1 over 6 is 10 over 60.
Now work along the tops: 30, take away 15, plus 12, take away 10. That leaves 17. So the first bracket is 17 over 60.
Second bracket. Here is a friendly pair: 2 over 5 and 3 over 5 make 1 whole. So we have 1, take away 5 over 9, take away 7 over 18.
In eighteenths, 1 is 18 over 18 and 5 over 9 is 10 over 18. Then 18 take away 10, take away 7, leaves 1. So the second bracket is 1 over 18.
Now we need 17 over 60, divided by 1 over 18. Dividing by 1 over 18 is the same as doing what?

ask.ifNot: Ask how many eighteenths fit into 1 whole: 18 of them. So dividing by 1 over 18 makes a number 18 times bigger.

beats.say: So it is 17 over 60, times 18. Divide the 60 and the 18 by 6, to get 10 and 3. Then 17 times 3 is 51, so we have 51 over 10.
51 over 10 is top-heavy. 10 goes into 51 five times, with 1 left over. So it is 5 wholes, and 1 over 10.
Big sums are just small sums in a row: one bracket, then the other, then the divide. And always look for friendly pairs, like 2 over 5 and 3 over 5.
We take the least number we can from 0.000326 so that a perfect square is left. Those zeros look scary, so let's hide them for a moment.
Look only at the digits 326. The square we land on must be below our number. So which square do we want?

ask.ifNot: We are taking away, so we move down. And to take away as little as possible, we stop at the nearest square below.

beats.say: 20 times 20 is 400: too big. Try 18. 18 tens are 180, and 18 eights are 144. Together, 324. Just 2 below 326!
And the next square, 19 times 19, is 361, which is above. So 324 is the square just below 326.
Now bring the decimal point back. Watch what squaring does to a decimal: 0.1 times 0.1 is 0.01. One decimal place becomes two.
324 is 18 times 18. With the decimal point back, the root is 0.018, which has 3 decimal places. How many decimal places will 0.018 times 0.018 have?

ask.ifNot: When we multiply decimals, the decimal places add up. 3 places and 3 places make 6 places.

beats.say: So 0.018 times 0.018 is 0.000324. Six decimal places, just like our number. That is the perfect square we land on.
0.000326 minus 0.000324 is 0.000002. That is the least number to subtract.
For a decimal like this, find the square hiding in the digits first. Then make sure the decimal places match, and line the digits up to subtract.
A tailor has 37.5 metres of cloth. From every metre he makes 8 pieces. How many pieces can he make in all?

board.text: 37.5 m of cloth. 8 pieces from each metre.

beats.say: Picture one metre of cloth, cut into 8 pieces. Then another metre, and 8 more. So what do we do with 37.5 and 8?

spec.note: Every metre gives 8 pieces

ask.ifNot: Each metre gives 8 pieces, again and again for every metre. 8 pieces, 37.5 times over, means multiply.

beats.say: 37.5 is 37 whole metres and half a metre. Take the whole metres first. 37 times 8 is 296.
Now the half metre. Half of 8 pieces is 4 pieces.
296 plus 4 is 300. So he can make 300 pieces.
Now look at the choices: 320, 360, 400, or none of these. Our 300 is not there! What should we do?

choices: check our sum, then trust it
ask.ifNot: A careful answer does not change just because it is missing from the list. We check it, and if it holds, we trust it.

beats.say: So let's check. 300 pieces, at 8 from each metre: 300 divided by 8 is 37.5 metres. Exactly the cloth he has.
Our answer is 300 pieces. Since 300 is not on the list, we choose none of these.
Two things to keep. Multiply when every one gives the same number. And if your checked answer is not listed, none of these is a real answer.
We want the least number that leaves 8 over when it is divided by 12, by 15, by 20 and by 54.
Take the left over 8 away from our number, and then 12, 15, 20 and 54 all divide it exactly. The least such number is their L C M.
Split each into primes. 12 is 2 times 2 times 3. 15 is 3 times 5.
20 is 2 times 2 times 5. And 54 is 2 times 3 times 3 times 3.
For the L C M, how many 3s do we need?

ask.ifNot: The L C M must hold all of 54, and 54 has three 3s. Those also cover the single 3s in 12 and in 15.

beats.say: So we take two 2s from 12, three 3s from 54, and one 5 from 15.
2 times 2 is 4, and 3 times 3 times 3 is 27. 4 times 27 is 108, and 108 times 5 is 540. So the L C M is 540.
Is 540 our answer?

ask.ifNot: 540 divides exactly, leaving nothing. We want 8 left over every time, so the number is 8 more than 540.

beats.say: 540 plus 8 is 548. That is the least number.
Check with 54: 54 times 10 is 540, and 8 more makes 548. Remainder 8, just as asked.
Same remainder with every divisor? Find the L C M of the divisors, then add the remainder.
One gross of notebooks is bought for 936 rupees. We need the cost of 48 notebooks.
There is a special word here: gross. How many is one gross?

ask.ifNot: A gross is a dozen dozens. That is 12 times 12, which is 144.

beats.say: A gross is a dozen dozens, and 12 times 12 is 144. So 144 notebooks cost 936 rupees.
Find one first. One notebook costs 936 divided by 144. Now, 144 times 6 is 864, and that leaves 72, which is exactly half of 144.
So 936 divided by 144 is 6 and a half. One notebook costs 6.50 rupees.
And how do we get the cost of 48 notebooks?

ask.ifNot: 48 notebooks, each costing 6.50 rupees. 48 lots of the same amount means multiply.

beats.say: 48 times 6 is 288. 48 times a half is 24. 288 plus 24 is 312.
So 48 notebooks cost 312 rupees.
Here is a lovely check. 48 is exactly one third of 144. So the cost should be one third of 936, and 936 divided by 3 is 312.
So unlock the special word first. Then find one, and then find many.
One number in this series is hidden behind the letter K: 9, 13, 21, 37, K, 133. Let's find the jumps.
From 9 to 13 is plus 4. What is the jump from 13 to 21?

ask.ifNot: 21 minus 13 is 8. So this jump is plus 8.

beats.say: Plus 8. And 37 minus 21 is plus 16.
The jumps are 4, 8, 16. What is happening to them?

ask.ifNot: From 4 to 8 is 4 more, but from 8 to 16 is 8 more, so it is not a steady add. Each jump is double the one before.

beats.say: Each jump is double the last. So the next jump is 16 times 2, which is 32.
37 plus 32 is 69. So K should be 69.
Let's make sure, using the last number. The jump after 32 is 64, and 69 plus 64 is 133. That matches the end of the series!
K is 69. But the choices are 79, 67, 63, or none of these. What do we pick?

ask.ifNot: We checked 69 against the 133 at the end, so we trust it. 69 is not on the list, so we choose none of these.

beats.say: 69 is not offered. So the right choice is none of these.
When your answer is not among the choices, check it once more. If it still holds, none of these is the right choice.
We take something from 1015 and must land on the greatest three-digit square number. So first, which square is that?
30 times 30 is 900. To step from one square to the next, add the two numbers: 900 plus 30 plus 31 is 961. So 31 times 31 is 961.
Step again: 961 plus 31 plus 32 is 1024. So 32 times 32 is 1024. Does that still have three digits?

ask.ifNot: 1024 has four digits, so it is too big. The last square with three digits is the one just before it, 961.

beats.say: So the greatest three-digit square is 961.
We start at 1015 and must come down to 961.
Which sum tells us what to subtract?

ask.ifNot: We want what must be taken from 1015 to leave 961. That is the gap between those two numbers.

beats.say: 1015 minus 961 is 54. So we subtract 54.
Check: 1015 minus 54 is 961, and 961 is 31 times 31. Find the target square first, then the gap.
A principal, the money at the start, earns 160 rupees of simple interest in 5 years, at 8 per cent per annum. We want the principal.

board.text: Interest Rs.160 in 5 years at 8% per annum

beats.say: Each year the principal earns 8 per cent of itself. Here are the 5 years, one at a time.
8 per cent every year, for 5 years. So the 160 rupees is what per cent of the principal?

ask.ifNot: Simple interest earns the same each year. 8 per cent, 5 times over, is 5 times 8, which is 40 per cent.

beats.say: 5 times 8 is 40. So 40 per cent of the principal is 160 rupees.
40 per cent is 4 lots of 10 per cent. So 10 per cent is 160 divided by 4, which is 40 rupees.
The whole principal is 100 per cent: 10 lots of 10 per cent. 10 times 40 is 400. So the principal is 400 rupees.
Careful: 160 is the interest, not the principal. The principal is the bigger sum that earned it.
Check: 8 per cent of 400 is 32 rupees a year. 5 years earn 5 times 32, which is 160. It works.
So for the principal: find what per cent the interest is altogether, then build up to 100 per cent.
This equation has a bracket on each side. We open the brackets first, and then we solve.
Left side first. The 4 multiplies both things inside. 4 times 2 x is 8 x. And careful: 4 times minus 1 is minus 4.
Now the right side. What does 5 times the bracket, x plus 2, open into?

ask.ifNot: The 5 multiplies the x and the 2. 5 times x is 5 x, and 5 times 2 is 10. So we get 5 x plus 10.

beats.say: So the bracket becomes 5 x plus 10, and the plus 4 is still waiting at the end.
10 and 4 are both plain numbers. Together they make 14.
x is on both sides now. What is a good next move?

ask.ifNot: We want the x terms together. The 5 x on the right is a plus 5 x, so we take 5 x away, from both sides.

beats.say: Take 5 x from both sides. On the right it is gone. On the left, 8 x take away 5 x leaves 3 x.
Undo the minus 4 by adding 4 to both sides. 14 plus 4 is 18, so 3 x equals 18.
Divide both sides by 3. 18 divided by 3 is 6. So x equals 6.
Check. Left: the bracket is 2 times 6, minus 1, which is 11. And 4 times 11 is 44. Right: the bracket is 8, and 5 times 8, plus 4, is also 44.
The plan: open every bracket, tidy each side, bring the letters together, clear the plain number, and divide last.
We need two primes: the greatest with two digits and the smallest with two digits. Then we square each and add.
The smallest first. The smallest two-digit number is 10. Is 10 prime?

ask.ifNot: 10 is 2 times 5, so it is not prime. 11 has no factors except 1 and itself, so 11 is the smallest two-digit prime.

beats.say: 10 is 2 times 5. 11 cannot be split, so the smallest is 11.
Now the greatest. Start at 99 and walk down. 99 is 9 times 11. 98 is 2 times 49. Neither is prime.
What about 97? It is odd. It does not end in 5. Its digits add up to 16, so 3 does not go in. And 7 times 14 is 98, so 7 just misses. Is 97 prime?

ask.ifNot: None of 2, 3, 5 or 7 divides 97 exactly. So 97 is prime, and it is the greatest two-digit prime.

beats.say: 97 is prime. So our two numbers are 97 and 11.
Now the squares. 11 squared is 11 tens plus one more 11: 110 plus 11, which is 121.
97 squared. 97 times 100 is 9700. That is 3 lots of 97 too many, and 97 times 3 is 291. So 9700 minus 291 leaves 9409.
Add the two squares: 9409 plus 121 is 9530.
Find each number, square each one, and only then add.

board.text: (Z + 41) is even. The 19th odd number before it?

beats.say: This one looks like algebra, but it is really about counting along a line of numbers.
We do not know Z, and we do not need to. Think of Z plus 41 as one even number, and walk backwards from it.

ask.ifNot: Even and odd numbers take turns. So the number right next to it, 1 less, is odd.

beats.say: What is the first odd number before any even number?
So the 1st one is 1 less. After that, each new odd number is 2 further back: 3 away, then 5 away.
To get from the 1st to the 19th takes 18 more jumps of 2. Careful: 18 jumps, not 19, because the 1st one is already counted.
18 jumps of 2 cover 36. Add the first step of 1, and we have gone 37 in all.
So the 19th odd number is 37 less than our starting number, Z plus 41.
Plus 41, then minus 37, leaves plus 4. So we have Z plus 4.
Try it with a real number. If Z is 1, then Z plus 41 is 42. Going back by 37 lands on 5. And 1 plus 4 is 5 too.
So the answer is Z plus 4. Remember: 1 step to reach the first one, then jumps of 2 for all the rest.
A square number is a number times itself. We are counting the squares that have 3 digits and are odd.
First, which squares have 3 digits? 10 times 10 is 100, the smallest 3 digit number. So we start at 10.
31 times 31 is 961, still 3 digits. But 32 times 32 is 1024, which is too long. So we stop at 31.

ask.ifNot: Odd times odd is odd, and even times even is even. So only an odd number has an odd square.

beats.say: Now, which numbers give an odd square?
So we need the odd numbers from 10 to 31. Here they are, starting at 11 and ending at 31.
Count along the list and you will find 11 numbers. Each one gives an odd square, so there are 11 odd squares with 3 digits.
Now look at the choices: 10, 12 and 13. Our 11 is not there!
So the answer is 'None of these'. Trust your working: when your number is not on the list, that is the right choice.
Something is added to 2 over 5, and the total is 5 over 2. What is that something?
How do we find the missing part of a sum?

ask.ifNot: If a part plus a missing part makes the total, then the missing part is the total take away the part we know.

beats.say: So we need 5 over 2, take away 2 over 5. Careful: they look alike, but they are flipped. 5 over 2 is 2 and a half, far bigger than 2 over 5.

spec.note: 5/2 is the top three bars together

beats.say: Halves and fifths are different sizes of piece. Which number do 2 and 5 both go into?

ask.ifNot: 7 is 2 plus 5, but we need a number in both times tables. 2 times 5 is 10, and 5 times 2 is 10.

beats.say: So we use tenths. 5 over 2 is 25 over 10, because top and bottom are both multiplied by 5. And 2 over 5 is 4 over 10.
25 tenths, take away 4 tenths, leaves 21 tenths.
21 and 10 share no factor except 1, so that is our answer: 21 over 10.
Check by adding back. 4 over 10 plus 21 over 10 is 25 over 10, and that is 5 over 2. It works.
To find what must be added: take the part you know away from the total, with matching bottom numbers.
An article worth 400 rupees is sold for 324 rupees. We want the loss as a per cent.

board.text: Cost price Rs.400, sold for Rs.324

beats.say: Two bars. The cost price, 400, is the longer one. The selling price, 324, is shorter, and the missing bit is the loss.
First the loss in rupees. 400 minus 324 is 76.
76 rupees were lost. To make that a per cent, we compare it with which amount?

ask.ifNot: Loss per cent, just as with profit per cent, is always worked out on the cost price. That is 400 rupees.

beats.say: Careful: it is the cost price, never the selling price. Now, per cent means out of every 100, and 400 is 4 hundreds.
So share the loss of 76 over the 4 hundreds. Half of 76 is 38, and half of 38 is 19. Each hundred loses 19 rupees.
19 lost out of every 100. So the loss is 19 per cent.
Check: 19 per cent of 400 is 4 times 19, which is 76. And 400 minus 76 is 324, the selling price.
So for a loss per cent: find the loss in rupees, then see how much that is for every 100 of the cost price.
A train 120 metres long runs at 36 kilometres per hour. In how many seconds will it pass a pole?
From the moment the front reaches the pole until the back end clears it, how far does the train travel?

ask.ifNot: The pole stays put, so the whole train has to slide past it. The train moves forward exactly its own length, 120 metres.

beats.say: So we need the time to travel 120 metres. But the speed is in kilometres per hour, and we want metres and seconds. Let's bring the speed down, one step at a time.
In 1 hour the train goes 36 kilometres. 1 kilometre is 1000 metres, so that is 36000 metres.
An hour is 60 minutes. Share 36000 metres over 60 minutes, and the train goes 600 metres in each minute.
A minute is 60 seconds. Share 600 metres over 60 seconds, and the train goes 10 metres in each second.
10 metres every second, and 120 metres to travel. What do we work out?

ask.ifNot: Each second takes care of 10 metres. Count how many lots of 10 fit into 120.

beats.say: 120 divided by 10 is 12. The train passes the pole in 12 seconds.
Check it. 12 seconds, at 10 metres each second, is 120 metres. Exactly one train length.
So for a train passing a pole: the distance is its own length, the speed goes into metres per second, and then time is distance divided by speed.
Three mixed numbers and a fraction add up to 34. The same number hides in every box. Let's call that number n.
Start with the whole numbers. 15 plus 10 plus 7 is 32.
The total must be 34, and the wholes give 32. So what must the fraction parts add up to?

ask.ifNot: The wholes already make 32. To reach 34 we need 34 take away 32 more, and that has to come from the fractions.

beats.say: 34 take away 32 is 2. So the four fractions together must make exactly 2.
All four fractions are seventeenths, so we add the tops: 7, and three boxes. And 2 wholes is 34 seventeenths, because 2 times 17 is 34.
So the tops must add up to 34. That is 7, plus 3 boxes, equals 34.
What do the 3 boxes add up to?

ask.ifNot: The 7 and the 3 boxes make 34 together. Take the 7 away from 34 to see what the boxes make on their own.

beats.say: 34 take away 7 is 27. So 3 boxes make 27, and one box is 27 divided by 3, which is 9.
Let's check. 7 plus 9 plus 9 plus 9 is 34, and 34 over 17 is 2. Then 32 plus 2 is 34. It works.
So the number in each box is 9. With mixed numbers, add the wholes and the fractions separately, then see what is still needed.
Four decimals made of 7s and 0s, placed to confuse the eye. Let's add them safely.
Before adding decimals, what must we line up?

ask.ifNot: Each digit must sit under digits of the same place: tenths under tenths, ones under ones. Lining up the points does exactly that.

beats.say: So write each one with three decimal places, padding with zeros. Now every point sits in the same spot.
Add two at a time. 7.007 plus 0.07 is 7.077.
Add 70.7 to that. The 7 tenths drop into the empty tenths place, and we get 77.777. All sevens!
Last, add 70.07. Take care with the carries: 7 tens and 7 tens make more than 10 tens, so 1 goes into the hundreds place. We get 147.847.
A rough check. 7 plus 70 plus 70 is 147, and our answer is just a little more than that. Good.
With decimals, line up the points, pad with zeros, and add place by place.
A student needs 40 per cent to pass. He scores 94 marks, and that is 74 marks short. We want the maximum marks.
He scored 94, and he was 74 marks short of passing. So what was the pass mark?

ask.ifNot: Being 74 short means he needed 74 more marks to reach the pass mark. So the pass mark is 94 plus 74.

beats.say: 94 plus 74 is 168. So he needed 168 marks to pass.
That pass mark is 40 per cent of the maximum. The maximum is the whole, 100 per cent. Picture it as 10 equal pieces of 10 per cent.

spec.note: 4 pieces = 168 marks

beats.say: 40 per cent is 4 pieces. So one piece is 168 divided by 4, which is 42.
The maximum is all 10 pieces. 10 times 42 is 420.
Check: 4 pieces of 42 make 168, the pass mark. He scored 94, and 168 minus 94 is 74. He is short by 74, as the question says.
So: first find the pass mark. Then use it as the per cent you know, and build up to the whole.

board.text: Rectangle: perimeter 96 cm, breadth = length − 6 cm

spec.note: Perimeter = 96 cm

beats.say: The perimeter of a rectangle is 96 centimetres, and its breadth is 6 centimetres less than its length. We want the area.

ask.ifNot: One length and one breadth take us exactly halfway round. So together they are half of 96.

beats.say: The perimeter is the walk all the way round: 2 lengths and 2 breadths. So what do one length and one breadth add up to?
Half of 96 is 48. So the length and the breadth together make 48 centimetres.
Now picture the two sides as bars. The breadth bar is 6 short of the length bar. If we give the breadth that extra 6, we have two equal bars, and together they make 48 plus 6, which is 54.

ask.ifNot: With the extra 6 added, there are two bars of the same size making 54. So one of them is half of 54.

beats.say: Two equal bars make 54, and each one is as long as the length. So what is the length?
Half of 54 is 27, so the length is 27 centimetres. The breadth is 6 less: 27 take away 6 is 21 centimetres.
Check before going on: 27 plus 21 is 48, just as it should be.
27 times 21 is easier in two pieces. Split the 21 into 20 and 1. First, 27 times 20 is 540.
And 27 times 1 is 27. Put the two pieces together: 540 plus 27 makes 567.
So the area is 567 square centimetres.
The trap is to halve 48 and call both sides the same. They are not equal: one is 6 longer. So deal with the difference first, then halve.
Fractions of numbers, a bracket, and a 2 standing right outside it. Remember that of means multiply.
Brackets first. Inside is 2 fifths of 40. How do we find 2 fifths of 40?

ask.ifNot: Fifths means sharing into 5 equal parts. So divide 40 by 5 to get one fifth, then take 2 of those parts.

beats.say: 40 divided by 5 is 8, and 2 of those make 16. And one ninth of 27 is 27 divided by 9, which is 3.
So the bracket is 16 plus 3, which is 19.
Now the front. 5 sixths of 72: 72 divided by 6 is 12, and 5 of those make 60.
We are down to 60 minus 2 times 19. Which part goes first?

ask.ifNot: The 2 next to the bracket means times, and times comes before minus. So 2 times 19 goes first.

beats.say: 2 times 19 is 38. And 60 minus 38 is 22.
Read of as times. Do the bracket first, then times, and the minus right at the end.
We are told Z is 7. One of these equations may be true for that Z. An equation is true when both of its sides come out the same.
So how do we test each one?

choices: put 7 in on one side only
put 7 in for Z on both sides
ask.ifNot: We put 7 in place of every Z, on the left and on the right, and then see whether the two sides match.

beats.say: A first. The left side is 5, plus 2 times 7, which is 19. The right side is 3 times 7, plus 2, which is 23. Not the same, so A is out.
Now B. The left side is 5 times 7, plus 6, which is 41. What is the right side, 7 Z minus 8?

ask.ifNot: 7 Z is 7 times 7, which is 49. Take away 8 and we get 41.

beats.say: 7 times 7 is 49, and 49 minus 8 is 41. Both sides are 41. B is true!
Let's be sure about C. The left side is 35 and the right side is 42. Not equal.
So the true equation is 5 Z plus 6 equals 7 Z minus 8.
To test an equation, put the number in on both sides and compare. Equal sides mean it is true.
Two numbers have H C F 13 and L C M 1989. One of them is 221, and we must find the other.
Here is the rule that unlocks this. For any two numbers, H C F times L C M equals the two numbers multiplied together.

board.text: HCF × LCM = first number × second number

beats.say: Put in what we know: 13 times 1989 equals 221 times the other number.
We could multiply 13 by 1989 straight away. But is there a neater way? Look at 221 and 13.

ask.ifNot: The H C F divides both numbers, so 13 must go into 221. Dividing first keeps every number small.

beats.say: 13 times 10 is 130. That leaves 91, and 13 times 7 is 91. So 221 is 13 times 17.
So 13 times 1989 equals 13 times 17 times the other number. The 13s cancel, and the other number is 1989 divided by 17.
17 times 100 is 1700, which leaves 289. And 17 times 17 is 289.
100 plus 17 is 117. So the other number is 117.
Check with the rule: 13 times 1989 is 25857, and 221 times 117 is 25857 too.
H C F times L C M equals the product of the two numbers. And cancel before you multiply: it saves a lot of work.
Mishti is facing South-West. She turns 180 degrees clockwise, and then 225 degrees anticlockwise. Which way is she facing at the end?

choices: a quarter of the way round
ask.ifNot: A half turn spins you round to face exactly the other way. It does not even matter which way you turn.

beats.say: We take one turn at a time. The first turn is 180 degrees, which is a half turn. Where does a half turn leave you facing?
A half turn leaves her facing the opposite way. The opposite of South-West is North-East.
Now the second turn, 225 degrees. The compass has 8 points, spaced evenly round a full turn of 360 degrees. So each step from one point to the next is 45 degrees.
How many steps of 45 make 225? 5 times 45 is 225. So she turns 5 steps.

ask.ifNot: Clockwise from North goes to North-East and then East. Anticlockwise is the other way round, so from North-East she goes back towards North.

beats.say: Those 5 steps are anticlockwise. Starting from North-East, which way does anticlockwise take her first?
Count 5 steps anticlockwise from North-East: North, North-West, West, South-West, South.
So Mishti is facing South.
Here is a quick check. 180 one way and 225 back the other way leaves just 45 degrees anticlockwise. And 1 step anticlockwise from South-West is South.
So for turning questions: take one turn at a time, and count in steps of 45 degrees round the compass.
This line is not true yet. One pair of brackets will make it equal 29.
Think backwards. If the plus 11 comes last, then everything before it must make 18. And there is a 36 in the line. What is 18 compared with 36?

ask.ifNot: 36 is 18 plus 18. So 18 is exactly half of 36.

beats.say: So we need half of 36. That means the part in front, 6 divided by something, should come to a half. 6 divided by 12 is a half.
Can we make 12 after the divide sign? Yes: 21 minus 9 is 12. So the brackets go round 21 minus 9.
Brackets first, giving 12. Then left to right: 6 divided by 12 is a half, and half of 36 is 18.
And 18 plus 11 is 29. The line is true now.
To place brackets, work backwards from the answer you need. Then look for numbers that can build the missing piece.
26500 rupees is deposited in a bank at 8 per cent per annum simple interest. We want the amount at the end of 4 years: everything that is there.

board.text: Rs.26500 at 8% per annum for 4 years

beats.say: 8 per cent means 8 out of every 100. So every 100 rupees earns 8 rupees in one year.

board.text: Every Rs.100 earns Rs.8 in 1 year

beats.say: 26500 divided by 100 is 265. So there are 265 hundreds, each earning 8 rupees a year.
265 times 8, in easy bites. 200 times 8 is 1600, 60 times 8 is 480, and 5 times 8 is 40. Together, 2120 rupees a year.
Simple interest earns the same every year. 4 years, each earning 2120. 4 times 2000 is 8000, and 4 times 120 is 480. So the interest is 8480 rupees.
Careful now. The question asks for the amount. Is 8480 the answer?

ask.ifNot: 8480 rupees is only the interest, the extra money. The amount is everything in the bank: the 26500 put in, plus the interest.

beats.say: 26500 plus 8480 is 34980. So the amount is 34980 rupees.
Check the interest with the formula: principal, times rate, times time, divided by 100. It gives 8480 too.
So: interest for one year, then for all the years. And when the question says amount, add the interest on to the money at the start.
A two-digit number ending in 8, times a three-digit number ending in 6. The other digits are hidden. Which choice can be the product?
We cannot multiply hidden digits. But what can we say for certain about the product?

ask.ifNot: The last digit of the product depends only on the last digits of the two numbers, and those are showing: 8 and 6.

beats.say: 8 times 6 is 48, so the product must end in 8. That removes 79764, which ends in 4.
The other three all end in 8, so now test the size. The smallest numbers that fit are 18 and 106, and 18 times 106 is 1908.
1808 is below the smallest possible product, so it is out.
The biggest numbers that fit are 98 and 996, and 98 times 996 is 97608. That has five digits, so the six-digit 970608 is far too big.
Only 50808 is left. And it works: 58 times 876 is 50808.
Two tests for a hidden-digit product: the last digit, and then the smallest and biggest it could be.
We are given that 6.7 times 58 is 388.6. The new sum has the same digits, with the points in different places.
How did 6.7 turn into 0.67?

ask.ifNot: The point moved one place to the left. That makes a number 10 times smaller, which is dividing by 10.

beats.say: 6.7 was divided by 10. And 58 became 5.8, so it was divided by 10 as well.
Both numbers are 10 times smaller. So the product is 10 times 10 smaller, which is 100 times smaller.
Dividing by 100 moves the point two places to the left. 388.6 becomes 3.886.
Does that feel right? About two thirds of nearly 6 should be close to 4. And 3.886 is.
Keep the digits from the fact you were given. Then work out how much smaller each number became, and shrink the answer by both.
The number is given in words: sixty-seven lakhs, ninety-four thousand, five hundred and twenty-one. First we turn it into digits.
In the Indian system we write it with commas like this: 67 for the lakhs, 94 for the thousands, then the last three digits.

ask.ifNot: Count them one by one: 6, 7, 9, 4, 5, 2, 1. That is 7 digits.

beats.say: How many digits does the number have?
7 digits, so the middle one is the 4th, with 3 digits on each side of it. That is the 4.
Now, which column is the 4 in? Units, tens, hundreds, thousands. It is in the thousands place.
4 thousands: 4 times 1000 is 4000.
Careful: the 9 beside it is in the ten-thousands place. They are neighbours, so it is easy to mix them up.
So the place value is 4000. Write the number in digits first, find the middle, then name its column.
The word solve here really means simplify. Three brackets are added together, and there are three families of letters: w, s and r.
Let's start with the w family. Which terms go with 4 w?

ask.ifNot: Like terms have the same letter. So 4 w goes with the other w terms: 2 w, and minus 3 w.

beats.say: 4 w plus 2 w is 6 w, and minus 3 w leaves 3 w.
Now the s family. 5 s minus 3 s is 2 s, and 4 s more makes 6 s.
Now the r family: minus 3 r, plus 2 r, plus 4 r. Careful with that first sign. How many r is that?

ask.ifNot: The first one is minus 3 r, so we start 3 below zero. Plus 2 brings us to minus 1, and plus 4 brings us up to 3. So 3 r.

beats.say: Minus 3, plus 2, plus 4 comes to 3. So that is 3 r.
Put the three families side by side: 6 s plus 3 w plus 3 r. The order does not matter, as long as each sign stays with its own term.
Test it with every letter as 1. The three brackets give 6, 1 and 5, which add up to 12. And 6 plus 3 plus 3 is 12 as well.
So to add long expressions: take one letter family at a time, and keep the sign in front of each term.
The sides of this triangle are written with the letter a: 3 a plus 5, 7 a plus 10, and 4 a plus 15. When a is 5, what is the perimeter?

ask.ifNot: A number written right next to a letter means times. So 7 a is 7 times 5, not 75.

beats.say: Wherever we see a, we put 5. But first: what does 7 a mean when a is 5?
The first side is 3 times 5, plus 5. 3 times 5 is 15, and 15 plus 5 is 20.
The second side is 7 times 5, plus 10. 7 times 5 is 35, and 35 plus 10 is 45.
The third side is 4 times 5, plus 15. 4 times 5 is 20, and 20 plus 15 is 35. Now every side has a real length.

ask.ifNot: The walk goes along every side, and a triangle has 3 of them. So we add all 3 lengths.

beats.say: Perimeter is the walk all the way round the triangle. Which sum gives it?
Add them one at a time. 20 plus 45 is 65. Then 65 plus 35 is 100.

spec.note: Perimeter = 100 units

beats.say: So the perimeter is 100 units.
Another way to check: add the letters first. The 3 sides together are 14 a plus 30. And 14 times 5, plus 30, is 100 too.
So: put the number in place of the letter to get each side, then add all 3 sides for the walk round.

spec.note: Perimeter = 84 cm

beats.say: The perimeter of a rectangle is 84 centimetres, and its breadth is half of its length. We want the length.
We do not know either side yet, so let's think in parts. Call the breadth 1 part. The length is twice as long, so it is 2 parts.

ask.ifNot: One length and one breadth make 3 parts, but that is only halfway round. The whole walk is 2 plus 1 plus 2 plus 1, which is 6 parts.

beats.say: Now walk all the way round the rectangle: a length, a breadth, another length, another breadth. How many parts is the whole walk?
The whole walk is 6 parts, and we know the walk is 84 centimetres. So 1 part is 84 divided by 6, which is 14 centimetres.
So the breadth, 1 part, is 14 centimetres. And the length, 2 parts, is 2 times 14, which is 28 centimetres.
Let's check the walk. 28 plus 14 is 42, and that is halfway. Double it: 42 plus 42 is 84. Just what we were told.
The question asks for the length. The length is 28 centimetres.
The trap here is 42. That is half the perimeter: the length and the breadth together, not the length alone.
A car travels 600 metres in 25 seconds. We want to know how far it goes in 1 hour.
25 seconds and 1 hour are far apart, so take a stepping stone: 1 second. How do we find how far the car goes in 1 second?

ask.ifNot: The 600 metres are spread evenly over 25 seconds. One second's share is 600 split into 25 equal parts.

beats.say: There are 4 lots of 25 in every 100. 600 is 6 hundreds, so that is 6 times 4, which is 24. The car goes 24 metres every second.
1 hour is 60 times 60 seconds, which is 3600 seconds. So we need 24 times 3600.
First 24 times 36. 20 times 36 is 720, and 4 times 36 is 144. Together, 864. Put the two zeros back: 86400 metres in 1 hour.
The choices are in kilometres. 1000 metres make 1 kilometre. What is 86400 metres in kilometres?

ask.ifNot: Dividing by 1000 moves every digit three places to the right. 86400 becomes 86.4.

beats.say: 86400 divided by 1000 is 86.4. So the car covers 86.4 kilometres in 1 hour.
Now look closely at the choices: 84.6, 80 and 85.4. Careful, 84.6 looks very like our 86.4, but the digits are swapped. Our answer is not on the list.
So the right choice is none of these. When your working is sound, trust it, even if the answer is not on the list.
Here is the plan again: go down to 1 second, build up to 3600 seconds, change metres to kilometres, then compare carefully with the choices.
A man buys a mobile phone for 18000 rupees: that is the cost price. He wants a profit of 18 per cent. What should the selling price be?
Two bars. The top one is the cost price, 18000 rupees. The selling price is longer, and the extra bit on the end is the profit.
The profit is 18 per cent. But 18 per cent of what?

ask.ifNot: Profit is always measured against the money paid at the start. That is the cost price, 18000 rupees.

beats.say: Careful: profit per cent is always worked on the cost price. For an awkward per cent such as 18, find 1 per cent first. 18000 divided by 100 is 180.
18 per cent is 18 lots of 180. 10 times 180 is 1800, and 8 times 180 is 1440. Together, 3240. That is the profit.
The profit is 3240 rupees. How do we get the selling price?

ask.ifNot: A profit means selling for more than was paid. So the profit is added on top of the cost price.

beats.say: 18000 plus 3240 is 21240. So the selling price is 21240 rupees.
Check with a rough guess. 20 per cent of 18000 would be 3600, so 18 per cent should be a little less. 3240 is. Good.
So for a profit: find the per cent of the cost price, then add it on. And when the per cent is awkward, go through 1 per cent.
Five numbers. We keep only the ones that 3 divides exactly, and then add those up.

ask.ifNot: For 3, the last digit does not help. Add up the digits: if the total is in the 3 times table, so is the number.

beats.say: What is the quick test for dividing by 3?
861: 8 plus 6 plus 1 is 15. 435: 4 plus 3 plus 5 is 12. Both totals are in the 3 times table, so we keep both.
218 gives 11, and 764 gives 17. Neither is a multiple of 3, so cross them out.
1263 gives 12. Keep it.
Now add the three we kept. 861 plus 435 is 1296. Then 1296 plus 1263 is 2559.
So the sum is 2559.
Test with the digit sum, keep the ones that pass, then add. Sorting first keeps the adding small.
The series goes 19, 31, 43, 55, and we want the 11th term.
What is the jump from each number to the next?

ask.ifNot: 31 minus 19 is 12. 43 minus 31 is 12. 55 minus 43 is 12.

beats.say: Plus 12, every time.
Think of the series as a staircase. We are standing on the 1st step, 19. To get to the 2nd step we climb once. To the 3rd, twice.
How many climbs to reach the 11th step?

ask.ifNot: We are already standing on the 1st step. So the climbs are 1 fewer than the step number: 10.

beats.say: 10 climbs of 12 each is 120.
19 plus 120 is 139. So the 11th term is 139.
Test the idea on the 4th term: 19 plus 3 climbs of 12 is 55. And 55 is 4th in our list.
If you use 11 climbs you get 151, one step too far. Find the jump, count 1 fewer, multiply, and add: 139.
The job here is to write the sentence as an equation. We do not have to solve it, only to build it, using W.
Consecutive means next to each other. Here are some odd numbers in a row: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. How far apart are neighbours?

ask.ifNot: From 3 to 5 we jump over the 4. So odd numbers that are neighbours are always 2 apart.

beats.say: So if the first odd number is W, the next one is W plus 2.
The question says the sum of the two numbers is 192. What does the word sum tell us to do?

ask.ifNot: Sum is the answer to an addition. So we add the first number and the next number.

beats.say: So we add them, and that must equal 192. W, plus W plus 2, equals 192.
Why not the others? W plus 2 equals 192 leaves out the first number. 2 W would mean two equal numbers. And W squared multiplies, when the word sum tells us to add.
Does our equation make sense? 95 and 97 are both odd, and they are neighbours. And 95 plus 97 is 192. It fits.
To turn words into an equation: name the first number, write the others from it, then follow the key word. Sum means add.
We subtract something from 13 times 14, and what is left must be the square of the smallest two-digit odd number.
Two things to find before we can subtract. First, 13 times 14. 13 tens are 130, and 13 fours are 52. Together, 182.
Second: the smallest two-digit odd number. The smallest two-digit number is 10. Is that the one we want?

ask.ifNot: 10 is even. The first odd number after it is 11, and that is the smallest two-digit odd number.

beats.say: Its square is 11 rows of 11. 11 tens are 110, and one more 11 makes 121.
So the question is now: 182, take away something, leaves 121.
How do we find the something?

ask.ifNot: If taking it away from 182 leaves 121, then it is the gap between 182 and 121. We subtract to find a gap.

beats.say: 182 minus 121 is 61. So we subtract 61.
Check: 182 minus 61 is 121, and 121 is 11 times 11. Work out each part of the sentence first, then find the gap.
Here is a line with two per cents, and a hidden number, A. We have to find A.
One of the per cents has no letter in it, so we can work it out straight away. That is 15 per cent of 40.
10 per cent of 40 is 4, and 5 per cent is half of that, which is 2. So 15 per cent of 40 is 4 plus 2: that makes 6.
So the line now says: 6, minus 25 per cent of A, equals 2.
6 minus something leaves 2. What is the something?

ask.ifNot: Start at 6 and come down to 2. You have taken away 4. So 25 per cent of A is 4.

beats.say: 6 minus 4 is 2. So 25 per cent of A must be 4.
25 per cent is one quarter. If a quarter of A is 4, then the whole of A is 4 quarters: 4 times 4, which is 16.

spec.note: 4 quarters make the whole of A

beats.say: Careful with that last step. A common slip is to take a quarter of 4. But 4 is already the quarter, so we multiply up, not down.
Check: a quarter of 16 is 4, and 6 minus 4 is 2. It works.
So work out the per cent you can, see what the missing per cent must be, then build up to the whole.
16 jugs can hold 1 decalitre of juice. How many jugs are needed to hold 15625 millilitres?
Two different units here, decalitres and millilitres. First, how much is 1 decalitre?

ask.ifNot: Deca means ten. So 1 decalitre is 10 litres.

beats.say: 1 decalitre is 10 litres, and each litre is 1000 millilitres. 10 times 1000 is 10,000 millilitres.
So 16 jugs hold 10,000 millilitres. Now both lines speak the same language.
Find one first. One jug holds 10,000 divided by 16, which is 625 millilitres.
Now, how many jugs of 625 millilitres do we need for 15625 millilitres?

ask.ifNot: We are counting how many times 625 fits into 15625. Counting how many times it fits is a division.

beats.say: 625 times 20 is 12500. 625 times 5 is 3125. Together they make 15625, so that is 20 and 5, 25 jugs.
We need 25 jugs.
Does it make sense? 15625 millilitres is more than 10,000, so we need more than 16 jugs. And 25 is more than 16.
So make the units match, find what one holds, then count how many you need.
We need the L C M and the H C F of 12 and 90, and then their sum. Prime factors give us both at once.
12 is even, so 2 comes out, and again. 12 is 2 times 2 times 3.
90 is 2 times 3 times 3 times 5.
First the H C F. Which primes do 12 and 90 share?

ask.ifNot: 12 has two 2s but 90 has only one, so one 2 is shared. 90 has two 3s but 12 has only one, so one 3 is shared.

beats.say: One 2 and one 3 are shared. 2 times 3 is 6, so the H C F is 6.
Now the L C M: every prime, the most times it appears. Two 2s from 12, two 3s from 90, and the 5. That is 4 times 9 times 5, which is 180.

spec.note: The L C M uses every prime in the picture, once each.

beats.say: A neat check: H C F times L C M should equal 12 times 90. 6 times 180 is 1080, and 12 times 90 is 1080 too.
Now add them. 180 plus 6 is 186.
Shared primes give the H C F. Every prime, the most times it appears, gives the L C M. Then do what the question asks.
Four big numbers to add. Before you start, look at the digits. Something is going on.
Read down each column of the table. What do you notice?

ask.ifNot: Read down any column. You will find a 1, a 2, a 3 and a 4, just in a different order each time.

beats.say: So every column adds up to the same thing: 1 plus 2 plus 3 plus 4, which is 10.
Units column: 10. Write 0, carry 1. Tens column: 10, plus the carried 1, is 11. Write 1, carry 1.
The hundreds do just the same: 11, write 1, carry 1. And the thousands make 11 as well, which we write in full.
Reading the digits off: 11110.
Another way to see it. Every place holds 10, so the total is 10 lots of 1111.
Before a big addition, look down the columns. A pattern can turn four long numbers into one small sum.
An equation with fractions. y, take away three quarters, equals 5 over 12 take away one third. We want y.
The right side is a sum we can finish, so let's tidy that first. 3 goes into 12, so one third is 4 over 12.
5 over 12 take away 4 over 12 is 1 over 12. Now the equation is much shorter.
y has three quarters taken away from it. How do we undo that?

ask.ifNot: Taking away is undone by adding. And to keep the balance level, we add three quarters to both sides.

beats.say: Add three quarters to both sides. On the left, y is alone. On the right we have 1 over 12 plus three quarters.
To add them we need twelfths again. Three quarters is 9 over 12. And 1 twelfth plus 9 twelfths is 10 twelfths.
10 over 12 can be simpler. What is the biggest number that divides both 10 and 12?

ask.ifNot: 10 is 2 times 5, and 12 is 2 times 6. So 2 goes into both.

beats.say: Divide the top and the bottom by 2. So y equals 5 over 6.
Let's check. 5 over 6 is 10 over 12. Take away 9 over 12 and we get 1 over 12, the same as the right side. It works.
Tidy each side first. Then undo what is done to the letter, doing the same to both sides.
Shraddha runs 5 rounds of a 400 metre track. In every round she runs the first 100 metres at 4 metres per second, and the other 300 metres at 5 metres per second. How long do the 5 rounds take?

board.text: Each round: 100 m at 4 m/s, 300 m at 5 m/s

beats.say: Every round is the same, so let's time just one round, in two parts, because she changes speed. First part: 100 metres, at 4 metres each second. How many seconds?

ask.ifNot: Each second she covers 4 metres. So we count how many lots of 4 fit into 100, and that is a division.

beats.say: 100 divided by 4 is 25 seconds. The second part works the same way: 300 divided by 5 is 60 seconds.
So one round takes 25 plus 60, which is 85 seconds. Notice we timed each part with its own speed. Dividing the whole 400 by one speed would not work, because the speed changes.
Now 5 rounds. 80 times 5 is 400, and 5 times 5 is 25. So 85 times 5 is 425 seconds.
The choices are in minutes and seconds. A minute is 60 seconds. So what is 425 seconds?

ask.ifNot: A minute is 60 seconds, not 100, so we cannot just split 425 into 4 and 25. Count in lots of 60 instead: 7 of them fit, and 5 seconds are left.

beats.say: 7 times 60 is 420. That leaves 5 seconds. So 425 seconds is 7 minutes 5 seconds.
Now look at the choices: 6 minutes 45, 7 minutes 15, and 7 minutes 25. Close, but none of them is 7 minutes 5 seconds.

board.text: Choices: 6 min 45 s, 7 min 15 s, 7 min 25 s

beats.say: So the right choice is none of these. Our working is sound, so we trust it.
The plan: time one round, a part at a time. Multiply by the number of rounds. Then change seconds into minutes using 60, not 100.

board.text: Square: same perimeter. Area of square = ?

beats.say: A rectangle is 22 metres long and 16 metres wide. A square has the same perimeter as this rectangle. We want the area of the square.

ask.ifNot: 22 plus 16 is only one length and one breadth, which is halfway round. We double it for the whole walk.

beats.say: Start with the rectangle's perimeter, the walk all the way round it. Which sum gives it?
22 plus 16 is 38, and that is halfway. Double it: 2 times 38 is 76. The rectangle's perimeter is 76 metres.
The square has the same walk round, 76 metres, shared among 4 equal sides. To divide by 4, halve and halve again. Half of 76 is 38, and half of 38 is 19.

ask.ifNot: The square shares the rectangle's perimeter, not its area. Its own area is its side times its side.

beats.say: So each side of the square is 19 metres. Now, which sum gives the square's area?
The area of a square is side times side.
19 times 19 is easier in two pieces. Split the 19 into 10 and 9. First, 19 times 10 is 190.
And 19 times 9 is 171. Put the two pieces together: 190 plus 171 makes 361.
So the area is 361 square metres. Now look at the choices: 324, 400 and 484. Our 361 is not among them.
When your answer is not on the list, check the working before you decide. 4 times 19 is 76, so the side is right. So the answer is: none of these.
So: perimeter of the rectangle, then the side of the square, then its area. And trust careful working, even when the list of choices does not have it.
A product on top, divided by a sum underneath. Let's write the top and the bottom separately.
Bottom first, it is easier. Pair the ends: 1 plus 8 is 9, and 2 plus 7 is 9 as well. Every pair makes 9. How many pairs do 8 numbers make?

ask.ifNot: Each pair uses up 2 numbers. So 8 numbers make 4 pairs.

beats.say: 4 pairs of 9 make 36. So the bottom is 36.
Now the top. Don't multiply it out yet! We are going to divide by 36, and 36 is 6 times 6. The top has a 6. Which two other numbers on top make another 6?

ask.ifNot: 2 times 3 is 6. So the 2, the 3 and the 6 on top multiply to 36 between them.

beats.say: So 2 times 3 times 6 is 36, and that cancels with the 36 underneath.
What is left on top? 1, 4, 5 and 7. 4 times 5 is 20, and 20 times 7 is 140.
The long way agrees. The top multiplies out to 5040, and 5040 divided by 36 is 140.
When a big product is divided by something, look for that something hiding among the factors. Cancel first, multiply after.
We need the L C M and the H C F of 48 and 120, and then the difference between them.
48 is even: halve it four times and 3 is left. So 48 is 2 times 2 times 2 times 2 times 3.
120 is 2 times 2 times 2 times 3 times 5.
For the H C F, how many 2s are shared?

ask.ifNot: 48 has four 2s, but 120 has only three. Shared means both numbers have it, so three 2s are shared.

beats.say: Ring three 2s and the 3 on the 48 line.
And the same on the 120 line. 2 times 2 times 2 times 3 is 24, so the H C F is 24.
Now the L C M. Take every prime the most times it appears: four 2s and the 3 from 48, and the 5 from 120. That is 48 times 5, which is 240.

spec.note: The L C M uses every prime in the picture, once each.

beats.say: Careful which is which. The L C M is the big one, 240. The H C F is the small one, 24.
240 minus 24 is 216.
Shared primes for the H C F. Every prime, the most times it appears, for the L C M. Then subtract the small one from the big one.
Here is a line with a hidden number, Z, and two per cents. We want Z.
Think of the equals sign as a balance. Before we can find Z, we turn each per cent into a plain number. Start with 16 per cent of 150.
10 per cent of 150 is 15. 5 per cent is half of that, 7.5. And 1 per cent is 1.5.
16 per cent is 10 and 5 and 1 together. 15 plus 7.5 plus 1.5 makes 24.
Now 13 per cent of 600. 1 per cent of 600 is 6, so we need 13 sixes. 10 sixes are 60, and 3 sixes are 18. Together, 78.
So our line becomes: Z plus 24 equals 78. Here it is on a balance.
Z plus 24 makes 78. How do we find Z?

ask.ifNot: Z and 24 together make 78. Take the 24 away from the 78, and what is left is Z.

beats.say: 78 minus 24 is 54. So Z is 54.
Check: 54 plus 24 is 78, and 78 is 13 per cent of 600. Both sides balance.
So with a line like this, turn each per cent into a plain number first. Then it is a simple missing number sum.
Some number, multiplied by the sum of 4 over 3 and 5 over 12, gives 9 over 7. We must find that number.
First the sum in the bracket. 3 goes into 12, so we change 4 over 3 into twelfths. 4 times 4 is 16, so it is 16 over 12.
16 over 12 plus 5 over 12 is 21 over 12. Then 21 and 12 both divide by 3, which gives 7 over 4.
So our puzzle is now: something, times 7 over 4, equals 9 over 7.
How do we undo times 7 over 4?

ask.ifNot: Times is undone by divide. So we take the 9 over 7 and divide it by 7 over 4.

beats.say: And to divide by a fraction, we flip it and multiply. Dividing by 7 over 4 is the same as multiplying by 4 over 7.
9 over 7 times 4 over 7. What do we get?

ask.ifNot: Multiply top by top, and bottom by bottom. 9 times 4 for the top, and 7 times 7 for the bottom.

beats.say: Tops: 9 times 4 is 36. Bottoms: 7 times 7 is 49. So the number is 36 over 49.
Let's check: 36 over 49, times 7 over 4. 36 divided by 4 is 9, and 49 divided by 7 is 7. That gives 9 over 7. It works.
Work out the bracket, then undo the multiplying by dividing. To divide by a fraction, flip it and multiply.
6420 rupees amounts to 10272 rupees in 4 years, at simple interest. We want the rate of interest per annum.

board.text: Rs.6420 amounts to Rs.10272 in 4 years

beats.say: 10272 rupees is the amount: the 6420 rupees at the start, with the interest on top.
So how do we find the interest?

ask.ifNot: The amount is the starting money and the interest together. Take the starting money away, and the interest is what is left.

beats.say: 10272 minus 6420 is 3852. So the interest is 3852 rupees, for all 4 years.
Careful: the rate is for one year, not for all 4. Simple interest is the same each year, so one year's interest is 3852 divided by 4, which is 963.
The rate is that 963 as a per cent of the starting money. 1 per cent of 6420 is 64.2. So how many lots of 64.2 make 963?
10 lots of 64.2 make 642. 5 lots are half of that, 321. And 642 plus 321 is 963. So it is 15 lots: the rate is 15 per cent.
Before we trust it, check with the formula: principal, times rate, times time, divided by 100. It gives 3852, our interest.
So the rate is 15 per cent per annum. Now look at the choices. Which one matches?

ask.ifNot: Our rate is 15 per cent, and that is not on the list. When careful, checked working matches none of the choices, the answer is none of these.

beats.say: So the answer is none of these. The rate is 15 per cent per annum, and that is not one of the choices.
So for the rate: find the interest, bring it down to one year, then see what per cent of the starting money it is.

board.text: Clock shows 12:45 p.m. Hour hand turns 214°.

beats.say: The clock shows 12:45 in the afternoon. Then the hour hand, the short one, turns through 214 degrees. What time is it now?

board.text: Hour hand: full turn = 360° in 12 hours

beats.say: The hour hand goes once round the clock, a full turn of 360 degrees, in 12 hours. 360 divided by 12 is 30. So it turns 30 degrees every hour.

ask.ifNot: 30 degrees are spread over 60 minutes. 30 is half of 60, so each minute gets half a degree. 6 degrees a minute is the speed of the minute hand.

beats.say: An hour is 60 minutes, and in that time the hour hand moves 30 degrees. So how far does it move in 1 minute?

board.text: Hour hand: 30° an hour, 1° every 2 minutes

beats.say: It moves half a degree a minute. Put the other way round: each whole degree takes the hour hand 2 minutes.
Now, how many whole hours are in 214 degrees? 7 thirties make 210. That leaves 4 degrees over.

ask.ifNot: Each degree takes the hour hand 2 minutes. So 4 degrees take 4 times 2 minutes.

beats.say: The 210 degrees are 7 whole hours. How long do the last 4 degrees take?
4 degrees, at 2 minutes each, is 8 minutes. So the hand has been moving for 7 hours and 8 minutes.
Add the 7 hours first. 7 hours after 12:45 is 7:45 in the evening.
Then the 8 minutes. 45 plus 8 is 53. The time is 7:53 in the evening.
So for the hour hand: 30 degrees is an hour, and each leftover degree is 2 minutes. Find the hours, then the minutes, then add them to the starting time.

board.text: (M + 46) is a 2-digit prime. The 19th even number before it?

beats.say: A letter in the question, but no need to worry. This is a counting puzzle in disguise.
First, a clue to decode. A prime with 2 digits cannot be even, because the only even prime is 2. So M plus 46 is an odd number.
We do not know M, and we do not need to. Think of M plus 46 as one odd number, and walk backwards from it.

ask.ifNot: Even and odd numbers take turns. So the number right next to it, 1 less, is even.

beats.say: What is the first even number before any odd number?
So the 1st one is 1 less. After that, each new even number is 2 further back: 3 away, then 5 away.
To get from the 1st to the 19th takes 18 more jumps of 2. Careful: 18 jumps, not 19, because the 1st one is already counted.
18 jumps of 2 cover 36. Add the first step of 1, and we have gone 37 in all.
So the 19th even number is 37 less than our starting number, M plus 46.
Plus 46, then minus 37, leaves plus 9. So we have M plus 9.
Try it with a real number. If M is 1, then M plus 46 is 47. Going back by 37 lands on 10. And 1 plus 9 is 10 too.
So the answer is M plus 9. Remember: 1 step to reach the first one, then jumps of 2 for all the rest.
We want every one digit factor of 48, all multiplied together. A factor of 48 is a number that divides 48 exactly.
Let's test each one digit number, 1 to 9.

ask.ifNot: 48 does not end in 0 or 5, so 5 does not divide it. But 6 times 8 is 48, so 6 and 8 both do.

beats.say: Which of these does not divide 48?
5, 7 and 9 do not divide 48, so cross them out. The factors left are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8.
Now multiply them, in friendly groups. 1 times 2 times 3 times 4 is 24. And 6 times 8 is 48.
So we need 24 times 48. 24 times 50 is 1200. That is 2 lots of 24 too many, so take away 48. We get 1152.
So the product is 1152.
List, test, cross out, then multiply in easy groups. And notice the 1: it is a factor, but it changes nothing.
Two jobs in this one. First we solve the equation to find p. Then we use p to work out p plus 3, times p plus 2.
p is on both sides. Which lot of p shall we take away from both sides?

ask.ifNot: Taking away the smaller lot, 2 p, keeps everything positive, and that is much easier to work with.

beats.say: Take 2 p from both sides. On the left only 5 is left. On the right, 9 p take away 2 p is 7 p.
Now undo the minus 30, by adding 30 to both sides. 5 plus 30 is 35.
7 p means 7 times p. Divide both sides by 7, and 35 divided by 7 is 5. So p equals 5.
Are we finished?

ask.ifNot: Look back at the question. It does not ask for p. It asks for the value of p plus 3, times p plus 2.

beats.say: Put 5 in for p. 5 plus 3 is 8, and 5 plus 2 is 7. 8 times 7 is 56.
Now look at the choices: 84, 14 and 36. Our 56 is not there. So the answer is none of these.
When your answer is not listed, check before you trust it. With p as 5, the left side is 2 times 5, plus 5, which is 15. The right is 9 times 5, minus 30, also 15.
So: solve for the letter, then answer what was really asked. And if your checked answer is not among the choices, none of these is the one to pick.
12 men can complete a job in 54 days. How many men are needed to complete the same job in 24 days?

board.text: 12 men finish the work in 54 days

beats.say: We want the job done faster, in 24 days and not 54. Will we need more men, or fewer?

ask.ifNot: To finish sooner, we need more hands on the job. More men.

beats.say: So the answer must be bigger than 12. Now, how big is the whole job? Let's measure it in days of work for one man.
12 men, each working 54 days. 12 times 50 is 600, and 12 times 4 is 48. So 12 times 54 is 648 days of work.

board.text: Whole job = 648 days of work for 1 man

beats.say: These 648 days of work must fit into 24 days. How do we find the number of men?

ask.ifNot: Each man can give 24 days of work. So we count how many times 24 goes into 648, and that is a division.

beats.say: 24 times 25 is 600. That leaves 48, which is 24 times 2. And 25 and 2 make 27.
So 27 men are needed.
Check. Both teams must do the same amount of work. 12 times 54 is 648, and 27 times 24 is 648 too.
The trap is to think fewer days means fewer men. Less time always needs more workers. Find the whole job, then share it out.
A bracket with fractions of numbers inside it, and then a divide by a fraction. One piece at a time.
Brackets first, and inside the bracket, of means multiply. How do we find 3 fifths of 25?

ask.ifNot: Fifths means sharing into 5 equal parts. So divide 25 by 5 to find one fifth, then take 3 of those parts.

beats.say: 25 divided by 5 is 5, and 3 of those make 15. In the same way, 39 divided by 13 is 3, and 7 of those make 21.
So the bracket is 9 plus 15, minus 21. That leaves 3.
Now we must divide 3 by 4 thirds. What is the trick for dividing by a fraction?

ask.ifNot: To divide by a fraction, turn it upside down and multiply. So dividing by 4 thirds becomes multiplying by 3 quarters.

beats.say: 3 times 3 quarters is 9 quarters.
8 quarters make 2 wholes, and there is one quarter more. That is 2 and a quarter, or 2.25.
Bracket first, reading of as times. And to divide by a fraction, flip it and multiply.
The series starts 26, 30, 34, 38, and it goes up by 4 each time. We want the 59th term.
The question gives us the jump, so let's mark it: plus 4, plus 4, plus 4.
See how the terms are built. The 2nd term is 26 plus one 4. The 3rd is 26 plus two 4s. The 4th is 26 plus three 4s.
2nd term, one 4. 3rd term, two 4s. 4th term, three 4s. So the 59th term is 26 plus how many 4s?

ask.ifNot: The number of 4s is always 1 fewer than the term number. For the 59th term, that is 58.

beats.say: 58 fours. 60 fours would be 240. That is 2 fours too many, so take away 8, which leaves 232.
26 plus 232 is 258. So the 59th term is 258.
A common slip is to use 59 fours. That gives 262, one jump too far.
The first term, plus the jump times 1 fewer than the term number. So the 59th term is 258.
Here is a right-angled triangle. We are not told its base or its height. We only know that its area is 18 times its base. We want the height.
We do know the rule for the area of any triangle: half of base times height. It is half of the rectangle drawn around it.
So now we have the same area written in two ways. They must be equal.

ask.ifNot: Both sides are something times the base. For them to be equal, the somethings must be equal: half of the height on the left, and 18 on the right.

beats.say: Look at both sides. Each one is something, times the base. What does that tell us?
The times base is on both sides, so we can cancel it from both. What is left is: half of the height equals 18.

ask.ifNot: If half of something is 18, the whole thing is twice as much. So we double 18.

beats.say: Half of the height is 18. So how do we get the whole height?
Double 18 is 36. So the height is 36 units.
Let's test it with a base of 10. Half of 10 times 36 is 180. And 18 times 10 is 180 too. It works.
So when the same thing multiplies both sides, cancel it. The trap here is to halve 18. Half of the height is 18, so the height itself is double.
We want to know what part of a whole day 216 minutes is, written as a decimal.
First we need a whole day in minutes. Which sum gives that?

ask.ifNot: A day has 24 hours, and each hour has 60 minutes. So it is 24 lots of 60.

beats.say: 24 times 60 is 1440 minutes in a day. So our fraction is 216 out of 1440.
Big numbers, so shrink it in steps. Divide the top and bottom by 12, and we get 18 out of 120. Divide by 6, and we get 3 out of 20.
Now turn 3 twentieths into a decimal. What should we change the 20 into?

ask.ifNot: Decimals count in tenths and hundredths. 20 goes into 100 exactly 5 times, so twentieths can be turned into hundredths.

beats.say: Multiply the top and the bottom by 5. 3 twentieths becomes 15 hundredths, which is 0.15.
Check: 0.15 of 1440 minutes should be 216 minutes. It is.
Put both amounts in the same unit, write the fraction, simplify it, and then change it to hundredths.
A principal, the money at the start, earns 2205 rupees of simple interest in 12 months, at 18 per cent per annum. We want the principal.

board.text: Interest Rs.2205 in 12 months at 18% per annum

beats.say: The rate is per annum, which means per year. How long is 12 months?

ask.ifNot: A year has 12 months. So 12 months is exactly 1 year, and 2205 rupees is one year's interest.

beats.say: 12 months is exactly 1 year. So 2205 rupees is one year's interest, and that is 18 per cent of the principal.

spec.note: The 18% piece is Rs.2205

beats.say: Here is a neat stepping stone. 18 per cent is 9 lots of 2 per cent. So 2 per cent is 2205 divided by 9.
9 times 200 is 1800. That leaves 2205 minus 1800, which is 405. And 9 times 45 is 405. So 2205 divided by 9 is 200 and 45: that is 245.
The whole principal is 100 per cent, which is 50 lots of 2 per cent. 100 times 245 is 24500, and 50 times is half of that: 12250.
So the principal is 12250 rupees.
Check: 18 per cent of 12250 should give back 2205, one year's interest. It does.
So: make sure the time is in years, then use the interest as a known per cent of the principal, and build up to 100 per cent.
We add 3042 and 869, then take a mystery number away, and we are left with 2165. What was taken away?
First the sum. Add the 869 in two bites. 3042 plus 800 is 3842, and 69 more makes 3911.
So we start at 3911, take something away, and land on 2165. How do we find the something?

ask.ifNot: Look at the bar. The whole is 3911 and one part is 2165. The other part is what is left when we take 2165 away from 3911.

beats.say: 3911 minus 2000 is 1911. Then take away the other 165, and we get 1746.
So the number to subtract is 1746.
Check by adding back. 1746 plus 2165 is 3911, our sum. It fits.
When a whole is split into two parts and you know one, subtract to get the other. A quick bar makes that easy to see.
Two lines here. The first is a fact: 4 x, minus 7, equals 12. The second is what we must find: 12 x, minus 14.
Start with the fact. What is in the way of the 4 x?

ask.ifNot: Look at the left side. The 4 x has a minus 7 hanging on to it. We clear that first.

beats.say: To undo minus 7 we add 7, on both sides. 12 plus 7 is 19. So 4 x equals 19.
We could divide by 4 now to find x. But look at what we need: 12 x. How is 12 x related to 4 x?

ask.ifNot: 12 is 3 times 4. So 12 x is 3 lots of 4 x. We do not even need to find x.

beats.say: So 12 x is 3 times 19, which is 57.
Do not stop there! The question wants 12 x, minus 14. 57 minus 14 is 43.
We can check by finding x after all. 4 x is 19, so x is 19 divided by 4, which is 4.75. And 12 times 4.75, minus 14, gives 43 again.
So before you solve for the letter, look at what is asked. Sometimes you can build it straight from what you already know.
Only a is given. m is built from a, and p is built from m. So we find them in order, and then compare three expressions.
Which letter can we find first?

ask.ifNot: p needs m, and m needs a. We know a, so m comes first.

beats.say: m is 7 minus 2, which is 5. Then p is 5 plus 5, which is 10.
First expression: m plus p is 15, and 15 times 7 is 105.
Second: p plus a is 17, and 17 times 5 is 85.
Third: a plus m is 12, and 12 times 10 is 120.
We have 105, 85 and 120. Careful now: what does the question want?

ask.ifNot: Read the question again. It asks which one has the least value, so we want the smallest.

beats.say: The smallest is 85, and that came from p plus a, times m.
So: find the letters in order, work out each expression with the bracket first, and check whether the question wants the greatest or the least.
An article sold for 336 rupees makes a loss of 84 rupees. We want the profit if the same article is sold for 542 rupees.

board.text: Sold for Rs.336: a loss of Rs.84.

beats.say: Both sales are of the same article. So the bridge between them is its cost price. We find that first.
It sold for 336 rupees, at a loss of 84. So was the cost price more than 336, or less?

ask.ifNot: A loss means it was sold for less than it cost. So the cost price is bigger than 336, by the 84 that was lost.

beats.say: 336 plus 84 is 420. So the cost price is 420 rupees.
Now sell the same article for 542 rupees. That is more than 420, so this time there is a profit. 542 minus 420 is 122.
Before we trust it, we check. 420 minus 84 is 336, the first sale. And 420 plus 122 is 542, the second sale. Both fit the question.
So the profit is 122 rupees. Now look at the choices. Which one matches?

ask.ifNot: Our profit is 122 rupees, and that number is not on the list. When careful, checked working matches none of the choices, the answer is none of these.

beats.say: So the answer is none of these. The profit is 122 rupees, and that is not one of the choices.
So the cost price is the bridge between two sales. And trust careful working, even when your answer is not on the list.
450 rupees is to become four times itself, at 24 per cent per annum simple interest. How long will it take?

board.text: Rs.450 becomes four times itself at 24% per annum

beats.say: The money becomes 4 times itself. How many lots of 450 must come from the interest?

ask.ifNot: There are 4 lots at the end, but 1 of them is the money we began with. So the interest must bring in the other 3 lots.

beats.say: That is the trap: one of the 4 lots is already there. So the interest needed is 3 times 450, which is 1350 rupees.

spec.note: 1 lot is the start, 3 lots are interest

beats.say: Now one year, at 24 per cent. 1 per cent of 450 is 4.5, so we need 24 lots of 4.5.
24 times 4 is 96, and 24 halves are 12. Together, 108. So one year earns 108 rupees.
How many years to earn 1350, at 108 a year? 10 years earn 1080. That leaves 1350 minus 1080, which is 270.
2 more years earn 216, which leaves 54. And 54 is exactly half of 108, so that is half a year more. 10 and 2 make 12 years, and a half.
Half a year is 6 months. So the time is 12 years 6 months.
Check: 12.5 years at 108 rupees a year comes to 1350, the interest we needed.
So when money becomes so many times itself, take away the lot you began with. The rest is interest: divide it by one year's interest.
A car travels 126 kilometres on 12 litres of petrol. How far will it go on 22 litres?
More petrol, so the car goes further. Our answer must be more than 126 kilometres.
What should we find first?

choices: how far it goes on 1 litre
ask.ifNot: Find one first. Once we know how far 1 litre takes the car, 22 litres is easy.

beats.say: 126 divided by 12. Now, 12 times 10 is 120, and the 6 left over is half of 12. So the car goes 10.5, ten and a half kilometres, on each litre.
And on 22 litres?

ask.ifNot: Every litre takes the car 10.5 kilometres, and there are 22 litres. 22 lots of 10.5 means multiply.

beats.say: 22 times 10 is 220. 22 times a half is 11. 220 plus 11 is 231.
The car will travel 231 kilometres.
Check another way. 22 litres is 12 litres and 10 more. The 12 litres give 126 kilometres, and 10 litres give 105. 126 plus 105 is 231.
Find how far one litre goes, then multiply by the litres you have. Find one, then find many.
This series goes down: 126, 124, 121, 116, 109, 98. We want the 10th term.
Let's write how much it drops each time. From 126 to 124 it drops 2. From 124 to 121 it drops 3.
What are the next three drops: 121 to 116, 116 to 109, and 109 to 98?

ask.ifNot: 121 minus 116 is 5. 116 minus 109 is 7. 109 minus 98 is 11.

beats.say: The drops are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11.
They are not the odd numbers, because 9 is missing and 2 is there. So what are they?

ask.ifNot: 2 is even and 9 is skipped, so these are not the odd numbers. Each one has exactly two factors: they are the primes.

beats.say: So the next drops are the next primes: 13, 17, 19, 23. We skip 15 and 21, because 15 is 3 times 5 and 21 is 3 times 7.
We have 6 terms and need the 10th, so 4 more drops. 98 minus 13 is 85. 85 minus 17 is 68.
68 minus 19 is 49. That is the 9th term, with one more drop to go. What is 49 minus 23?

ask.ifNot: Take away 23 in two steps: first the 2 tens, then the 3 ones.

beats.say: 49 minus 23 is 26. So the 10th term is 26.
49 is one of the choices, but it is only the 9th term. Count your terms as you go. The 10th is 26.
Three steps: find two special numbers, multiply them, then find what the 6 in the answer is worth.
The greatest 3 digit number is easy. It is 999.

ask.ifNot: 99 can be divided by 9, and 91 can be divided by 7. 97 cannot be divided by anything, so it is the greatest 2 digit prime.

beats.say: Now the greatest 2 digit prime. Which is it?
So we need 97 times 999.
999 is just 1 less than 1000. So take 97 thousands, and then take away one 97. That leaves 96903.
Now find the 6 in 96903. Units, tens, hundreds, thousands. It is in the thousands place.
6 thousands: 6 times 1000 is 6000.
So the place value of the 6 is 6000. Multiplying by 999 is easy when you think of it as 1000 take away 1.
We want the smallest three-digit number whose three digits are all different. Then we square it.
The smallest three-digit number is 100. But look at its digits: 1, 0, 0. The 0 is used twice.
Next is 101. Does that work?

ask.ifNot: 101 has the digits 1, 0, 1. The 1 appears twice, so it is out.

beats.say: 101 is out. Then 102: its digits are 1, 0 and 2. All different! So our number is 102.
Now square it: 102 times 102. Break the second 102 into 100 and 2.
102 times 100 is 10200. 102 times 2 is 204. What is 10200 plus 204?

ask.ifNot: Line up the place values: the 204 sits under the last three digits of 10200. Then add column by column.

beats.say: 10200 plus 204 is 10404. So the square is 10404.
Does that make sense? 100 squared is 10000, and 102 is a little bigger than 100. So a little more than 10000 is just right.
Read every condition: smallest, three digits, all different. Only then square.
The L C M of two numbers is 882 and their H C F is 14. One number is 98. Which number is its partner?
There is a rule that links all four. H C F times L C M equals the first number times the second number.

board.text: HCF × LCM = first number × second number

beats.say: So 14 times 882 equals 98 times the other number.
Before multiplying big numbers, look for something to cancel. How many 14s are in 98?

ask.ifNot: Count up in 14s, or try 14 times 7. It lands exactly on 98.

beats.say: 98 is 14 times 7. So 14 times 882 equals 14 times 7 times the other number, and the 14s cancel.
That leaves 882 divided by 7. 7 times 100 is 700, which leaves 182. And 182 is 7 times 26.
100 plus 26 is 126. So the other number is 126.
Check with the rule: 14 times 882 is 12348, and 98 times 126 is 12348 as well.
So when you know the H C F, the L C M and one number: use the product rule, and cancel before you multiply.
We are given a multiplication fact, but asked a division with decimals. The digits match, so the fact will do the heavy work.
First turn the fact into a division. Which division does it give us?

ask.ifNot: If 168 lots of 54 make 9072, then 9072 shared into 168 equal parts gives 54 in each.

beats.say: So 9072 divided by 168 is 54. Now for the decimal points.
9072 became 0.9072: the point moved four places, so it was divided by 10000. And 168 became 16.8, divided by 10.
The number being shared is 10000 times smaller, so the answer shrinks 10000 times. But the divisor is 10 times smaller too. What does a smaller divisor do to the answer?

ask.ifNot: Sharing among fewer gives each one more. So when the divisor gets 10 times smaller, the answer gets 10 times bigger.

beats.say: 10000 times smaller, then 10 times bigger. Overall, the answer is 1000 times smaller than 54. That is 0.054.
Check by multiplying back. 16.8 times 0.054 gives 0.9072. Just right.
In a division, shrinking the first number shrinks the answer, but shrinking the divisor makes the answer grow. Track both.
Which fraction equals 259 over 333? Big numbers, but there is a neat way in.
The choices are 148 over 222, 55 over 77, 77 over 99, and 56 over 108.
333 is a friendly number: it is 9 times 37. Let's see if 37 goes into 259 as well.
Try 37 times 7. What does it make?

ask.ifNot: Work it out on paper: 7 times 37. You will find it lands exactly on 259.

beats.say: So 259 is 7 times 37, and 333 is 9 times 37. Divide the top and the bottom by 37, and the fraction is 7 over 9.
Now we want a choice that also simplifies to 7 over 9. Look at 77 over 99. Both numbers are in the 11 times table.
So what is 77 over 99 in its simplest form?

ask.ifNot: 77 divided by 11 is 7, and 99 divided by 11 is 9. Keep the top on top, and the bottom on the bottom.

beats.say: 77 over 99 is 7 over 9 as well. That is our match.
The others do not match. 148 over 222 is two thirds, 55 over 77 is 5 over 7, and 56 over 108 is 14 over 27.
With big fractions, hunt for a number that goes into both the top and the bottom. Simplify, and equal fractions show themselves.
An article is sold at a loss of 12 per cent, and that loss is 60 rupees. We want the profit per cent if it is sold at 620 rupees instead.
A loss per cent is always a per cent of the cost price. So this tells us that 12 per cent of the cost price is 60 rupees.
What is the handiest stepping stone to the whole cost price?

ask.ifNot: We know that 12 per cent is 60 rupees. Share the 60 into 12 equal parts, and each part is 1 per cent of the cost price.

beats.say: 60 divided by 12 is 5. So 1 per cent of the cost price is 5 rupees.
The whole cost price is 100 per cent. 100 times 5 is 500 rupees.
Now it is sold at 620 rupees. That is above 500, so there is a profit: 620 minus 500 is 120 rupees.
For the profit per cent, we compare the 120 rupees with which amount?

ask.ifNot: Profit per cent is always worked out on the cost price. Here that is 500 rupees.

beats.say: 1 per cent of the cost price is 5 rupees. How many 5s make 120? 120 divided by 5 is 24. So the profit is 24 per cent.
Check: 24 lots of 5 rupees: 20 times 5 is 100, and 4 times 5 is 20, which makes 120. The working holds.
Now look at the choices. 24 per cent is not among them. So the answer is none of these.
So: use the loss to find the cost price, then take the new profit per cent on that cost price. And trust careful working, even when it is not on the list.
What per cent is 84 minutes, of 7 hours?
Before we compare them, what must we fix?

ask.ifNot: 84 is in minutes and 7 is in hours. We can only compare two amounts when they are in the same unit.

beats.say: Careful: 84 divided by 7 would mix minutes with hours. Change the hours into minutes first. Each hour is 60 minutes, so 7 hours is 7 times 60: 420 minutes.
So the real question is: 84 minutes is what per cent of 420 minutes? Here are the 420 minutes, cut into 10 equal pieces of 10 per cent.

spec.note: 10 equal pieces: each is 10%

beats.say: One piece is 10 per cent of 420. Divide by 10: that is 42 minutes.
One piece is 42 minutes. How many pieces make 84 minutes?

ask.ifNot: 42 and 42 make 84. So 84 minutes is 2 of the 10 per cent pieces.

beats.say: 42 plus 42 is 84. So 84 minutes is 2 pieces of 10 per cent, and that is 20 per cent.

spec.note: 2 pieces of 42 minutes = 84 minutes

beats.say: Check: 20 per cent is one fifth, and 420 divided by 5 is 84. It fits.
So for what per cent is this of that: put them in the same units first, then see how many 10 per cents fit.
We build the smallest 5 digit even number from 7, 4, 3, 6 and 9. Then we read off its hundreds digit.
Even means it ends in an even digit. Ours are 4 and 6, so one of them goes last.

ask.ifNot: If 4 went last, we could not use it near the front, where it keeps the number small. So we save the 4 and put 6 at the end.

beats.say: The smallest digit, 3, goes first. We would like 4 to come next. So which even digit should go last?
3, then 4, then 7 and 9 in rising order, and 6 at the end. That makes 34796.
Compare it with putting 4 at the end. The best we could do then is 36794, and ours is smaller.
Now the hundreds place. Units, tens, hundreds: the third digit from the right is 7.
So the digit in the hundreds place is 7.
Choose the last digit so that the small digits stay free for the front. Then count the places from the right.
We need the first four two-digit prime numbers. Then we square each one, and add the squares.

board.text: Squares of the first four two-digit primes, added

beats.say: Start at 10 and test each number. 10 is even. 11 is prime. 12 is even. 13 is prime.
14 is even. What about 15?

ask.ifNot: 15 is in the 5 times table: 3 times 5. So it is not prime.

beats.say: 15 is 3 times 5, so we skip it. 16 and 18 are even. That leaves 17 and 19. So our four are 11, 13, 17, 19.
Now square each. 11 squared is 110 plus 11, which is 121. 13 squared is 130 plus 39, which is 169.
17 squared is 170 plus 119, which is 289. 19 squared is 190 plus 171, which is 361.
Four numbers to add: 121, 169, 289, 361. Which pairing makes the adding easy?

ask.ifNot: Look at the last digits. 1 and 9 make 10, so 121 plus 169 ends in a zero. So does 289 plus 361. Round numbers are easier to add.

beats.say: 290 plus 650 is 940. So the sum of the squares is 940.
List the primes, square each one, then pair up friendly numbers to add.
This line is not true yet. One pair of brackets will make it equal 19.
As it stands, we go left to right: 42 divided by 7 is 6, times 2, plus 16, comes to 28. Too big.
Think backwards from 19. If the plus 16 comes last, then just before it we had 3. So 42 divided by something must be 3. Divided by what?

ask.ifNot: 3 times 14 is 42. So 42 divided by 14 gives 3.

beats.say: We need to divide by 14. And 7 times 2 is 14! So the brackets go round 7 times 2.
Brackets first: 7 times 2 is 14. Then 42 divided by 14 is 3.
And 3 plus 16 is 19. The line is true now.
Here is something worth noticing. Divide and times are equally strong, so without brackets the divide on the left goes first. The brackets let the times jump the queue.
To place brackets, work backwards from the answer, and find which numbers can build the piece you need.
These are Roman numerals, so the pattern is in disguise. Let's turn each one into an ordinary number first.
Remember the letters. I is 1, V is 5, X is 10, L is 50 and C is 100.
The first numeral is X, C, then V, I, I. An X before a C means 10 less than 100, which is 90. Then V, I, I adds 7. So what is the first number?

ask.ifNot: A smaller letter before a bigger one is taken away. So X before C is 90, not more than 100. Then add the 7.
